name: Southside
description: Gin, lime, mint, and sugar—essentially a gin Mojito served up.
history: Associated with early-20th-century American bars and Prohibition-era lore. The mint-lime-gin combination is the point; the stories are optional.
whyItWorks: Mint oils and lime brighten gin; sugar keeps the sour from turning austere. Served up, it feels more composed than a Mojito.

ingredients.label: Mint leaves
ingredients.notes: Required for the drink’s identity; confirm mint is on hand.

steps: Gently clap or lightly muddle mint with simple syrup in the shaker—do not shred the leaves.
Add gin, lime juice, and ice.
Shake hard and double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a fresh mint sprig.
techniqueNotes: Overmuddling mint turns the drink grassy and bitter.
Double-strain to keep leaf fragments out of the coupe.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Gunpowder tea and mint are a natural pairing.
Cucumber-rose gin leans into the herbal side.
Clean juniper keeps mint and lime in focus.

variations.name: Southside Fizz
variations.notes: Strain over ice and top with club soda.
